title: Cold wax medium finish on air-dry clay
subtitle: Applying cold wax medium over sealed air-dry clay for a soft, diffused surface
excerpt: Cold wax medium rubbed into a sealed air-dry clay surface gives a soft, semi-opaque finish that settles into recessed texture, creating depth and a tactile quality different from acrylic paint or varnish alone. Layers can be built up and partially wiped back for varied effects. No kiln is required.
sourceNotes: Cold wax medium application derived from established mixed-media techniques.

glossaryTerms.definition: A paste of bleached beeswax dissolved in mineral spirits that acts as a painting medium and surface finish; applied without heat

content.text: Unlike gloss varnish, which sits on top of a surface,

penetrates slightly and gives a soft, buffed finish. On textured clay it pools in the low points and remains thinner on raised areas, naturally emphasising surface relief. It can be mixed with oil paint for tinted effects or used clear over an acrylic base layer.

materials.name: Bone-dry air-dry clay piece, sealed with two coats of PVA
Oil paint, raw umber (optional, for tinted wax)

content.text: Work in a ventilated room as cold wax medium contains mineral spirits. Scoop a small amount onto the hake brush. Apply across the clay surface in broad strokes. Do not overwork: two or three passes per area is enough for one coat.
Allow the first coat to harden for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Buff with a clean dry cloth in circular motions. The surface should feel smooth and slightly waxy, not tacky.

Apply a second coat mixed with a small amount of raw umber oil paint to add warmth. Wipe back immediately with the cloth to leave colour only in the recessed areas. Buff once dry. Repeat for additional depth.

After the final coat hardens for at least 1 hour, buff the whole surface vigorously with a fresh dry cloth until the surface takes on a low-sheen lustre. The wax is cured well enough for display use after 24 hours, but reaches full hardness after 5 to 7 days.

items.problem: Surface stays tacky after 30 minutes and will not buff
items.cause: Too much wax was applied in one coat; it cannot harden evenly
items.fix: Wipe off the excess with a clean cloth while it is still soft. Next coat, apply a very thin layer and buff more vigorously

items.problem: Tinted wax leaves ugly streaks rather than settling into texture
items.cause: The oil paint proportion was too high relative to the wax
items.fix: Use only a very small amount of oil paint relative to the wax: a ratio of about 1:8 paint to wax is usually enough for a tinted effect. More paint makes the mix behave like paint, not wax
